subject: GDPR: DPA & SCC selection \u2014 Acme integration
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acme.com>, Tom Berger <tberger@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: GDPR: DPA & SCC selection — Acme integration

Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciate the thoughtful questions on data flow and legal requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side related to GDPR / DPA / SCC: 

- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report (security). Attached is a 1-page summary. We can share the full report under NDA if you need it.
- DPA: We have a DPA template we typically start from. I attached a draft (Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf). 
- SCCs: For cross-border transfer, we can execute the EU SCCs using the standard Module Two (Controller-Processor) or Module Three (Processor-Processor) as applicable. From our product flow, Redwood will act as a processor for customer data in this integration (we don't set policy for Acme data). See the SCC selection matrix attached.
- Vendor security questionnaire (VSQ): Rishi will fill out your VSQ; if there are specific sections your legal team cares most about (e.g., data retention, subprocessor list, encryption at rest), call them out and we'll prioritize.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm that Acme intends to treat Redwood as a processor for this integration.
2) If confirmed, we'll send a DPA + SCCs (Module Two) for your review and Rishi will return the completed VSQ by EOD tomorrow.
3) If your legal wants the full SOC 2 under NDA, we can do that in parallel.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf, SCC_selection_matrix.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from legal:

- Acme's preference is to have Redwood contractually confirmed as a processor (we control purposes/means). Please confirm in the DPA.
- For SCCs, our legal prefers Module Two (Controller-Processor) unless there's a strong reason to use another module.
- We've attached Acme's Vendor Security Questionnaire — please have your security team complete and return.

Can you confirm whether Redwood maintains a published subprocessor list and whether you support customer-requested data deletion (and confirmation) for GDPR requests?

If we can get the DPA + SCCs and the completed VSQ this week, procurement can start the review next week.

Regards,

Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GDPR: DPA & SCC selection — Acme integration

Elena — great, thanks for the clarity. Confirmations and updates below: 

- Controller/Processor role: Confirmed — Redwood will be a data processor for Acme data in this integration. The DPA draft reflects that.
- SCC Module: We agree Module Two (Controller-Processor) is the appropriate set for cross-border transfers — included in the DPA draft.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessor list (link included below). We also have a process to notify customers of new subprocessors and support contractually-required approvals where necessary.
- Data deletion: We support customer-initiated deletion requests and can provide confirmation once deletion is completed; retention periods are configurable per customer.

I've attached the DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf) and an SCC selection matrix that maps our typical roles and recommended modules (SCC_selection_matrix.xlsx). Rishi will complete the VSQ and send answers in a separate email.

Next steps:
- Rishi to return the completed Acme_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire by EOD tomorrow.
- If Acme legal wants the full SOC 2, reply here and we'll initiate an NDA to share the report.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena / Acme legal —

Attached are our responses to the Acme Vendor Security Questionnaire (see answers in-line in the PDF). High-level answers to the questions you flagged: 

- Subprocessor list: Published and available at https://redwood.com/subprocessors (we included the current list in the questionnaire).
- Encryption: Data is encrypted at rest and in transit; keys managed via customer KMS where requested.
- Retention & deletion: Customers can request deletion; we confirm completion via system logs and a signed confirmation if required.

Attachments: Redwood_VSQ_answers_Acme.pdf

If you need anything more from our security team, happy to connect Vivek for a short call.
